transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just been feeling really weighed down by this sense that I’ve messed things up. Like with my family — I took on this mortgage, and I keep thinking I’ve trapped us or let them down somehow. Even if nothing huge happens, it just sits in my head like, “What were you thinking?”

And then at work, I’m a waiter, so small mistakes happen — forgetting something for a table, being a little slow, getting an order slightly wrong — but lately every little thing feels like proof that I’m useless. I know people probably see it as just a normal mistake, but to me it turns into this whole thing, like I deserve whatever bad comes from it because I should’ve done better. It’s been hard to shake that feeling.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting the same enjoyment out of things you used to like — maybe hobbies, time with friends, or even just relaxing?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not always like I’m sad about every single thing, exactly, but things just don’t pull me in the same way.

Like at work, I used to actually enjoy parts of it — not the rushing around maybe, but I’d joke with the regulars, remember little things about them, have a bit of back-and-forth. Sometimes that was the thing that made the shift feel okay. Lately I catch myself just keeping my face kind of straight, saying what I need to say — “Can I get you anything else,” “I’ll be right back” — and then I move on. I don’t feel that little spark to make a joke or keep a conversation going.

And after shifts, I used to text my brother sometimes, just dumb stuff from the day or complain about a weird customer or whatever. Now I’ll see his message and just… leave it there. Not because I’m mad at him. I just don’t feel that pull to answer. It feels like too much somehow, even when it’s not. So yeah, I guess enjoyment is part of it, but it’s also like I’m more blank and disconnected from things I used to naturally do.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or run down lately, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

I don’t know that I’d say I’ve noticed that in a clear way. Like, I get tired after a shift, but I’m on my feet a lot, carrying plates around, running back and forth, so that kind of makes sense to me. I haven’t really been thinking, “Why am I exhausted when I didn’t do anything?”

Maybe I feel kind of worn down mentally sometimes, but I’m not sure if that’s the same thing you mean. Physically, I don’t think there’s been some big change where I’m suddenly drained all the time. It’s more… I don’t know, I’d have to pay attention to it more, I guess.
Have you found it harder to focus or make decisions lately — like, maybe even simple things take more effort to figure out?

Yeah… yeah, actually. That one I have noticed more, especially at work. It’s not like I can’t think at all, but stuff that should be automatic feels… shaky, I guess.

Like using the POS system — I’ve been doing this for years, putting in orders, splitting checks, closing things out — and lately I’ll enter something and then just stare at the screen like, “Did I do that right?” Even if I literally just typed it in. I’ll go back and check the numbers, and then I don’t trust the checking either, so I’ll check again. It’s embarrassing, because it’s such basic stuff for the job.

And inventory sheets too, when I have to keep numbers straight — counts, totals, whatever — I’ll look at the page and it’s like the numbers don’t stay put in my head the way they should. I’m not saying I’m completely unable to do it, but it takes more effort, and I second-guess myself way more than I used to. Sometimes I’m just sitting there with the screen in front of me, knowing I know how to do this, but not feeling confident that what I entered is actually right.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… it’s been kind of uneven. I wouldn’t say I’ve been carefully tracking my weight or anything, so I don’t know if I’ve lost a certain amount. But my eating has definitely been all over the place.

Some weeks at work, we’ll have staff meal or there’ll be food around, and I’ll look at it and just not really want it. I’ll pick at a few bites or tell myself I’ll eat later, and then later comes and I still don’t really bother. It’s not always that I feel sick or anything — it’s more like food just doesn’t seem worth the effort.

But then other nights I get home and it’s the opposite. I’ll just start eating whatever’s in the kitchen — leftovers, bread, cereal, random stuff — not because I’m really enjoying it, but because it feels like I’m trying to settle myself down somehow. Like if I’m full maybe I’ll feel more grounded or less… I don’t know, unsettled.

So it’s not a clean “I’m eating less” thing every day. It swings around. Some days barely anything, some nights too much, and I haven’t really known what to make of that.
Have you been feeling down or having a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I would have called it “depressed” right away, because I still get up and go to work and do what I’m supposed to do, so part of me keeps thinking, well, maybe I’m functioning, so maybe it’s not that bad. But most days there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest.

It’s like I’m carrying it around with me while I’m carrying plates and checking on tables and smiling at people because that’s the job. I can do the smile, I can say the right things — “How’s everything tasting?” and all that — but it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Not because I feel friendly or happy or anything good, just because I know I’m supposed to act that way.

And it’s not necessarily dramatic every second, like I’m crying all day or something. It’s more this flat, weighed-down feeling that keeps coming back and sitting there. Most of the day, most days, yeah.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down or that you're moving more slowly than usual, like things take more effort or time to process?

Yeah… I think people at work have noticed it more than I wanted them to, honestly. It’s not always one direction, which is part of why it feels weird to explain. Sometimes I’m moving too much, like I’ll keep circling back to the same section, checking the same tables even when I already checked them, looking at the same receipts, making sure I didn’t miss something. I’ll walk from the dining room to the POS, then back again, then realize I’m basically pacing and not actually getting anything new done.

But other times it’s the opposite. Like I’ll need to grab menus or go enter something in the POS, and it’s like my body takes a second longer to start moving. Not frozen exactly, just… delayed. I’ll know what I’m supposed to do, but getting from “I need to do that” to actually doing it feels slower than it should. Even walking over to the station or getting receipts together can feel like it takes more effort than normal.

And I’ve had coworkers kind of give me looks, not in a mean way, more like they can tell I’m either over-checking everything or I’m dragging. It makes me self-conscious, because waiting tables is all timing, you know? You’re supposed to be quick and smooth, and lately I don’t feel quick or smooth.
Have you ever had a period of time before this one — lasting at least a couple of weeks — where your mood was low or you felt similar to how you’ve been feeling lately?

Yeah… I mean, there have been times before where I’ve felt something like this. I’m trying to think how to explain it without making it sound more exact than it is, because I don’t sit there with a calendar marking it off, you know?

But yeah, I’ve had stretches where most days felt heavy in that same way. Like this empty feeling sitting in my chest, and I’m still showing up, still carrying plates, still smiling at tables and saying the things I’m supposed to say, but it doesn’t feel like it’s coming from anywhere real. It’s more like I know the script, so I follow the script.

And it’s strange because from the outside I probably look like I’m doing okay enough. I’m working, I’m talking, I’m moving around. But inside it’s just… flat. Like I’m going through the motions because that’s what’s expected, not because I feel anything good. So yes, I’d say I’ve had periods before that felt similar.

Can you recall if you’ve had at least one other period in your life, before this current one, where your mood was low for most of the day, nearly every day, and you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in most activities, lasting for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I’m not great with the exact timeline, like I can’t point to a clean start date and end date, but there have definitely been other stretches before this where it felt like most days had that same heavy, empty feeling.

It’s like I’d still be doing everything I was supposed to do — going in for shifts, carrying plates, checking on tables, smiling at customers — but it didn’t feel like I was actually there in a real way. More like I knew the routine, so I just kept doing the routine. The smile was there because the job needs it, not because I felt good or interested or connected to anything.

And the enjoyment part… yeah, I guess that fits too, because even things that should have felt nice just kind of didn’t land. It all felt flat. I’d get through the day, but it was more like pushing myself through it than actually wanting to be part of anything.

So, yes, I’d say I’ve had at least one other period like that, where it was most of the day, most days, and it went on long enough that it wasn’t just a bad couple of days.
